newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgarian parliament speaker backs election call.
newsitem.headline: Bulgarian parliament speaker backs election call.

text.p: The speaker of Bulgaria's parliament, Blagovest Sendov, said on Sunday the ruling Socialist party should agree to opposition demands for a general election.

"The Democratic Left should show wisdom and show that it cares for Bulgaria, and it should hold negotiations with the United Opposition under the condition of early parliamentary elections," said Sendov, who supports the Socialists in parliament.

"If this condition is in place, a new government will be formed in Bulgaria and the opposition will continue working in the parliament, because it is clear that measures to stabilise Bulgaria could be taken only by a working parliament," Sendov told the national television in an interview.
President Zhelyu Zhelev said he would ask the Socialists to form a new government only if they agreed to hold elections.
"I will give a mandate for forming a government only when the political forces agree on an early parliamentary election," Zhelev told the national radio.
Tens of thousands of people from the capital and the provinces rallied in Sofia on Sunday, the seventh consecutive day of protests calling for elections.
